My father and I hadn’t spoken for the last two years.
Amaia Santa Ana — interview

I wanted to close the foundation, because I knew it was dirty. He called it ‘your grandfather’s legacy’. Last week he called me, the first time in two years. ‘You were right,’ he said. ‘Tomorrow I’m taking everything in.’ I’m the heir, yes; but last night I was in Madrid. I came on the first train this morning.
She turns the silver ring on her finger.
Why weren’t you speaking to your father?

A file reopened from the archive (June 1989, closed as an ‘accident’):

· Gaspar Santa Ana (61) was found drowned in the palace cistern; the cover open. ‘He went down at night to cool off and fell.’
· The steward’s statement that day: ‘There was a lady with him.’ That sentence is crossed out, with a note in the margin: ‘witness mistaken’.
· A week later the board of trustees of the Fundación Santa Ana (founded 1985) made Dr Edda Varga chief adviser; the same month a large ‘donation’ came into the foundation from Napoli, via Caruso Marittima.
· The name of the officer who closed the file appears two years later on the foundation’s bursary list.
· The foundation’s 1994 staff record: ‘Mercedes Llorente, intern — on Dr Varga’s recommendation.’
The file closed as an ‘accident’ forty-one years ago has been reopened.
THE 1989 FILE — FERNANDO SANTA ANA

· Cause of death: drowning; a metre of water in the cistern.
· From the six-metre fall, right collarbone and wrist broken; no heavy blow to the head, he was conscious when he fell.
· Lime from the cistern wall under the nails: he tried to climb.
· On the back, between the shoulder blades, a faint bruise the size of two hands.
· Time of death: 23.30–01.00.

Steward

The same cistern. I was twenty-six. That night too there was a woman with him, a foreigner, fair-haired; Mr Gaspar said to her, ‘Edda, no,’ I heard it. In the morning they said ‘accident’. A week later the board made her chief adviser. For forty-one years I kept quiet. Ms Mercedes is that woman’s hand here.
He doesn’t take his eyes off the orange tree in the courtyard.
What happened to Don Gaspar in 1989?
Steward.
I open and close the door of this house.

All day Don Rodrigo prepared a file in the study, a thick file. Towards eleven at night Ms Mercedes said, ‘I’ll show you something,’ and they went down to the courtyard. Only two people have the cistern key: me and Ms Mercedes. Mine was in my drawer. In the morning I saw the scarf.
He checks the buttons of his waistcoat one by one.
What happened in the courtyard last night?
Isidro Navas — interview
Deputy director.
For thirty years the foundation has given this city schools, a boathouse, an archive.
No.
His father said no as well. Edda never forgets being told no.

Rodrigo said, ‘I’m finished with E. V.,’ he prepared a file, he was going to go to bube. I called Edda; she said, ‘Remember Gaspar,’ that was all. I opened the cistern for him and said, ‘Your father hid something here.’ He leaned down. I pushed. I locked the cover, burnt the file in the fireplace, put the key in the hidden compartment. Then I sent a message. No reply came. It never does.
You pushed Rodrigo into the cistern.
Rodrigo was tired; he wanted some air. He had the cistern opened; he wanted to look. It had been his obsession since his father. I left him there and went upstairs.
She touches her pearl earring and lowers her hand.
Why did you go down to the courtyard last night?
In 1989 I was thirteen. Don’t pin that on me.

SANTA ANA  /  MURDER
The director of the foundation that has passed along the edge of every file in this chapter was found dead in his palace’s cistern.
FILE #059

Mercedes Llorente’s office in the palace and the fireplace (with the branch chief’s approval):

· In the hidden compartment of the writing desk, the key to the cistern cover; fresh lime and moss on the key’s tip, Mercedes Llorente’s fingerprint on it.
· In the fireplace ash, a thick, half-burnt file: the auditor’s tables and the slips for the reinsurance payments to Montreal.
· On her phone, 28 October 23.51, to an unregistered number: ‘Sevilla is closed.’ No reply. 1,140 messages to the same number since 1994.

On the morning of 29 October 2030, at the Palacio Santa Ana in Triana, the director of the Fundación Santa Ana, Rodrigo Santa Ana (66), was found dead in the old cistern beneath the courtyard. The cistern’s iron cover was locked.

The steward Isidro Navas found the body at 07.30 when he saw a scarf hanging from the edge of the cover. In the palace that night: deputy director Mercedes Llorente and financial auditor Héctor Bermejo worked until late. The victim’s daughter Amaia Santa Ana arrived in the morning.

The day before, the victim had called bube Sevilla — Triana branch and made an appointment for 29 October at 10.00.

The steward, the daughter and the auditor told of the night and of 1989; those got the archive opened. The camera showed the woman locking the cover. The search found the key in the hidden compartment and the file’s ashes in the fireplace.
Father and son said the same word. The answer was the same for both.
Palacio Santa Ana — October 2030

In 1989 Gaspar Santa Ana said to a woman, ‘Edda, no,’ and died in the cistern; a week later Dr Edda Varga became the foundation’s chief adviser and Napoli money began to flow. For thirty years the foundation made the donations behind Sevilla’s dirty dealings and passed the returns to Montreal. His son Rodrigo decided to take everything to bube. The deputy director Mercedes Llorente took him down to the courtyard, pushed him into the cistern, locked the cover and burnt the file.
Who killed Rodrigo Santa Ana?
